name: Don's Heating & Cooling LLC
website: none found (no company website in any search result; presence is directory listings only)
what_they_do: Small owner-operated HVAC contractor doing furnace repair, HVAC installation, maintenance and service calls for Spotswood-area homes. Reviews consistently describe a single owner-technician ('Don') handling the work himself.
customers: Homeowners and small property owners in Spotswood and nearby Middlesex County towns needing repair, replacement or seasonal maintenance.

size_signals.signal: Reviews describe one owner-technician doing the work; 25 reviews on a claimed Birdeye profile with published hours (Mon-Fri 9-5, Sat 9-3)
No website; contact is a single phone number (732-385-7446) and a Spotswood address in a residential circle - consistent with a home-based one-van operation (inference)

listing.platform: Birdeye (claimed profile, includes Google reviews; live Google rating not directly confirmed)

website_review.out_of_date_signs: No owned web presence at all: the only 'profile' is third-party directory pages (Birdeye, BestProsInTown, Cylex-type aggregators), several of which cannot be verified as current
website_review.search_basics: Nothing to optimise - no site, so no titles, service pages or schema; searches for the business return only directories
top_issues: No website: a homeowner comparing three HVAC quotes has nothing to read, no licence/insurance statement, no service list, no reviews on an owned page
No online quote or appointment request - every job starts with a phone call the owner has to answer while on a ladder
Information lives on aggregator pages the owner does not control, with inconsistent data across them

agent_readiness.notes: Findable: a claimed Birdeye profile carries hours and 25 reviews, and the business appears on several local directories, but there is no Google Business Profile confirmed and no website to crawl. Answerable: nothing on an owned domain - no services, service area, price ranges or hours in readable text, and no schema.org markup anywhere. Bookable: phone-only; no form, no calendar, so a customer's agent has no way to request service.

operations_signals.signal: Every job intake is a phone call to a one-person operation that is often on site; reviews praise response times, which suggests the owner is absorbing all scheduling himself
Published hours are Mon-Fri 9-5 plus Sat 9-3, so calls outside those windows have no capture path at all

top_opportunities.opportunity: Build a five-page site (home, services, service area, about/licence, quote request) with click-to-call and a labelled quote form that emails the owner - the single biggest gap
top_opportunities.evidence: No website exists in any search result; all information sits on third-party directory pages

top_opportunities.opportunity: After-hours intake agent: answer/return missed calls and web enquiries with service-area and availability questions, then book a callback slot
top_opportunities.evidence: Phone-only intake, hours 9-5 Mon-Fri and 9-3 Sat, one owner-technician doing the work

top_opportunities.opportunity: Google Business Profile cleanup plus post-job review requests (the 4.2 average with only 25 reviews is the visible weak spot versus Spotswood competitors)
top_opportunities.evidence: 4.2 across 25 aggregated reviews with positive sentiment in the summaries - volume and average both look improvable

scores.reasons: Gap: no website, no form, no booking, no schema - almost nothing to build on. Pay: one-person HVAC shop, high job value (installs) but small budget and no marketing spend visible. Ease: a brochure site plus a form is a short job. Evidence: strong on existence and review data from directories, weaker on the Google profile and revenue because there is no first-party site.
